_why: Row 106: the boundary is a MANIFEST, not a naming convention. Every served method states its wire identity, direction, producer/consumers, shapes, refusals, and profiles. No wildcard consumer role: unbuilt callers are named as such. IRI redirects are UNPUBLISHED (row-105 W3ID caveat) -- these IRIs are intent, not resolvable identity. Profiles are [] throughout: no method is mapped to OSI profiles yet, and mapping is future work, not a guess. The 3-class ontology (Application/Operation/RefusalReason) is NOT published here -- that needs a W3ID stewardship pledge, which is an owner act.

Proposed (UC_GameSurface). HTTP POST /_cpcp/rpc on the game seam (Bun, default 127.0.0.1:8787). Every call needs a credential the IQ gate's /whoami names (Bearer, or the box's own on loopback): unauthenticated / seam_unreachable. Refusals ride HTTP 200; with header cpcp-http-status-profile: dual-v1, failure_layer http_request -> 400 and infrastructure -> 500. Auth refusals carry failure_layer http_auth (contract PR #11); under dual-v1, unauthenticated is HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and the rest 403 (iq@f9f1b80e). IRI as the seam's own CID declares it (game#game.catalog), not the registry's prefix-stripped form (game#catalog).

methods.note: Proposed (UC_SharedSurface contract, slice 9 backend). Served only on the game seam's POST /_cpcp/rpc: translated before dispatch into the native game method, so the gate (card:game:<native>), journal, receipts and refusals are the native method's. The facade's own refusals (no_such_method, grounding_refused, not_supported) are answered before dispatch, always HTTP 200, without asking the gate who the caller is. `surface` names the session (s-<id> or iq:game:session:<id>); `driver` is accepted and unused. Answered by surface.js itself (describe()), no native method and no credential check. A method of the shared-surface contract (UC_SharedSurface contract.json), answered on the game seam's own endpoint by its surface facade (seam/surface.js), translated to the seam's native method before dispatch.

The facade's own refusals (no_such_method, grounding_refused, not_supported) are answered before dispatch, always HTTP 200, without asking the gate who the caller is. `surface` names the session (s-<id> or iq:game:session:<id>); `driver` is accepted and unused. Native method: session.join. A method of the shared-surface contract (UC_SharedSurface contract.json), answered on the game seam's own endpoint by its surface facade (seam/surface.js), translated to the seam's native method before dispatch.
